![text](12,820,112,909) Schema of DB must be known at first program & written for embedded SQL ![text](12,909,112,977) → can get info at runtime instead of compile time ![list](12,977,112,1037) - SALSTATE - common effect not offered here ![text](12,1037,112,1105) EXEC SQL SELECT S-name, S-age INTO :c-name, :c-age FROM S-ids S WHERE S-ssd = :c-ssd ![text](12,1105,112,1172) → in parameter ![list](12,1172,112,1240) - for db, start index from 1 ![list](376,17,476,103) - Improbable Mismatch problem ![list](376,103,476,172) - Fixed with Cursor ![text](376,172,476,240) OPEN: when SQL statement is executed ![text](376,240,476,308) FETCH: when it moves to the next row ![text](376,308,476,376) INSSENSITIVE Cursor: cannot make changes to DB with Cursor. ![text](376,376,476,444) If I want to update result, then declare SENSITIVE Cursor ![text](376,444,476,512) → Fixes issue with collecting set of tuples ![text](376,512,476,580) CLOSE: closes the cursor ![text](376,580,476,648) Cursor can be reopened when in variable is different ![text](376,648,476,716) Note the poll question !! ![text](376,716,476,785) - execute Update () ![text](376,785,476,853) (number of rows selected) ![list](722,17,822,103) - to make any changes, I need to declare a sensitive Cursor ![text](722,103,822,172) - embedded SQL recommended in systems that require high performance without JDBC overhead ![text](722,172,822,240) - for dynamic SQL, we cannot reuse, since we need to prepare ![text](722,240,822,308) JDBC/JDBC ![text](722,308,822,376) JDBC does not require knowing details of schema info ![text](722,376,822,444) - can connect to multiple DBs with multiple separate drivers ![text](722,444,822,512) - all interactions with the DB performed via a Connection Object ![text](722,512,822,580) Prepared Statement is more efficient to use since it is made to reuse as it is precompiled ![text](722,580,822,648) - ? are placeholders ![text](722,648,822,716) - Keyword → Redundancy
